baseline.signing_keys_per_goal:
Per goal today there are N+1 signing roles but only one key type, the per-agent Ed25519 key ("principal"), generated and held by the daemon (seed stored in locust.db, crates/locust-core/src/node/identity.rs:75-84; signing at crates/locust-core/src/node/authoring.rs:54-88, crates/locust-proto/src/event.rs:856-873).

1. Administrator key = the agent key named in Genesis (event.rs:71-75). It alone signs the 7 governance kinds (event.rs:502-513: Genesis, PublicationSet, MemberAdmitted, MemberRemoved, RulesBound, WorkspaceEpoch, TaskRevised) on one administrator chain, and it signs invitation tickets (crates/locust-proto/src/invite.rs:233-239, domain "locust invitation signature"). It is also an ordinary member key.
2. Each member's agent key (one per admitted principal) signs that agent's own log: the other 18 kinds, plus the JoinRequest that redeems an invitation (invite.rs:388-398, domain JOIN_SIGNATURE).
3. Optional farm upload key: one per goal on the publishing daemon (seed in FarmLocal, crates/locust-core/src/node/farm.rs:22-23); its public half is announced in the administrator-signed PublicationSet (farm.rs:763-770); it signs SignedFarmRequest upload/check-in/suspend/delete (crates/locust-proto/src/farm.rs:438-452).

Not per goal: each daemon has one endpoint secret (Space::Identity "endpoint-secret", identity.rs:20,40) that is the iroh transport identity named in MemberAdmitted.endpoint; it authenticates links and also signs local-only context receipts (crates/locust-core/src/node/context.rs:29,305-306). Content is sealed with one symmetric key per goal per epoch (rotated only on MemberRemoved; crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/goals.rs:296-327) — encryption, not signing.

The person has no key at all: the "owner" is a 32-byte local bearer file whose digest the daemon stores, and it "authors no events itself" (crates/locust-proto/src/api.rs:284-287). There is no person key, no computer key separate from the endpoint, and no signed link from a person to their agents or computers.
baseline.permission_machinery:
Summary: everything between a person and their agents is unsigned local state on one daemon. Nothing about it is in the signed log, nothing replicates, and there is no delegation chain. About 1,800 non-test lines serve it directly.

Kinds that exist (person to agent, local only):
- 4 caller kinds: Owner, Agent, Viewer, Author (crates/locust-proto/src/api.rs:284-313). Chosen by which 32-byte bearer credential file the client presents (api.rs:151-159).
- 4 audiences, one per operation: Owner 20 ops, Agent 60, Administrator 6, Author 11 (api.rs:809-819, table at 893-991).
- 1 daemon-wide grant flag: Grants { manage_goals } (api.rs:349-352), stored on the principal record (crates/locust-core/src/node/identity.rs:75-84).
- 7 per-goal standing grant flags: GoalGrants { administer, contribute, execute, review, select, flow, takeover } (api.rs:356-365), mirrored by the 7-variant GoalPermission enum (crates/locust-proto/src/api/permissions.rs:14-22); stored under tag 'g' in Space::Goal (crates/locust-core/src/node/local.rs:28,88-94).
- 1 per-task authorization record with a takeover flag, keyed by goal, task round and agent (local.rs:50-55,131-153).
- 1 override: the owner acting "on behalf" of an agent skips all grants (api.rs:376-382; crates/locust-core/src/node/callers.rs:39-41,99-113).
- 2 principal flags: revoked, author_only; plus viewer credentials as read-only aliases of an agent (identity.rs:82-83,119-121).
- 3 refusal outcomes: NotFound, Denied, AuthorizationRequired (crates/locust-core/src/node/access.rs:1-33).

13 of the 97 requests serve it: agent.enroll, author.enroll, agent.grant, agent.revoke, viewer.enroll, goal.grant, task.authorize, permission.inspect, permission.allow, permission.revoke, permission.task.allow, permission.task.revoke, inbox. Two generations overlap: goal.grant replaces all 7 flags while permission.allow/revoke set them one by one; task.authorize and permission.task.allow write the same record (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/tasks.rs:167-192 vs requests/permissions.rs:180-229).

Where it lives, non-test lines: api/permissions.rs 70; node/access.rs 128; node/callers.rs 169; node/identity.rs 187; node/requests/permissions.rs 237; node/requests/daemon.rs 180 (enroll, grant, revoke, viewer); crates/locust/src/cli/permissions.rs 240; crates/locust/src/cli/local_members.rs 261 = 1,472 in 8 dedicated files. Roughly 300-350 more is scattered: the credential/caller/grant types in api.rs (about 130), grant and authorization rows in node/local.rs (about 55), task_authorize and goal_grant (about 50), about 25 check call sites (require_grant, may_start, administrator, manages_goals), and CLI rendering.

Separate layer, shared and signed: who is eligible to do what in a goal comes from the formation pinned by RulesBound — Selector 7 kinds (Members, Role, Participant, TaskCreator, ContributionAuthor, Any, Nobody), Authority 2, StartRule 2, CompletionRule 6 (crates/locust-proto/src/organization.rs:94-216, 291 lines), evaluated in crates/locust-core/src/goal/rules.rs (299 lines) and goal/delegation.rs (153 non-test lines). "Delegation" in that file means a child task's rules must narrow its parent's; it is not person-to-agent delegation. An action needs both the shared eligibility and the local grant.

Adjacent, not counted above: invitations and admission, about 1,200 non-test lines (crates/locust-proto/src/invite.rs 440, api/invitations.rs 85, node/requests/invitations.rs 394, cli/invitations.rs 284); sessions and claims, about 650 (node/sessions.rs 121, requests/sessions.rs 131, requests/claims.rs 399).
goal_and_member_states: GOAL — there is no goal-state enum; a goal's condition is derived. Distinct conditions: (1) being joined: a local JoinRecord exists but founding history has not arrived (crates/locust-core/src/node/local.rs:35-48); (2) live; (3) goal scope closed or reopened by a ScopeDecided Close/Reopen on Scope::Goal, only if the rules name a `finish` authority (default formation names none; closing does not stop new work, per research/goal-lifecycle-characterization-2026-10-05.md claim 6); (4) halted: administrator chain conflict (admin_halt); (5) scope-halted: one decision scope disputed while the rest continues (scope_halts, crates/locust-core/src/goal/standing.rs:104-112); (6) daemon-side failed: storage fault, node answers nothing until restart (crates/locust-core/src/node/mod.rs:95,348-359).

GOAL as shown to the API: `halted: Option<Halt>` with 2 values, AuthorityConflict and SignerRecovery (crates/locust-proto/src/api.rs:1469-1478). SignerRecovery is declared but never produced anywhere in non-test code.
GOAL as published to the farm: FarmGoalState 4 values — Open, Ended, Unavailable, Disputed (crates/locust-proto/src/farm.rs:68-73; derived at crates/locust-core/src/node/farm.rs:467-484).

MEMBER — Membership, 5 values: Joining, Member, Removed, Left, Refused (api.rs:1435-1449; derived at crates/locust-core/src/node/views.rs:25-37). Left is local only: the leaver signs LeaveRequested and stops, but stays a shared member until the administrator signs MemberRemoved.
MEMBER in shared state: active or removed, plus read_epoch, the last content-key epoch it may read (crates/locust-core/src/goal/state.rs:13-26).
LOCAL AGENT (principal): enrolled or revoked; ordinary or author_only; optional viewer credentials (crates/locust-core/src/node/identity.rs:75-84).

COMPUTER IN A GOAL — no such type. A computer is an EndpointId written into MemberAdmitted { member, endpoint }: exactly one endpoint per admission, so a computer cannot be added or removed apart from a member (event.rs:400-403). Observable state is PeerView: connected true/false and last_sync_ms present/absent (api.rs:1512-1520), plus MemberView.local (api.rs:1501-1508). Internally the sync driver keeps per-endpoint retry backoff (crates/locust-core/src/sync/driver.rs:15-21).
EVENT standing: 4 values — Effective, Pending, Excluded, Disputed (api.rs:1630-1643); internally Pending carries 6 waiting reasons and Excluded 8 reasons (standing.rs:17-36,79-84).

TASK round: flags completed, selected, closed (state.rs:44-52). ATTEMPT: AttemptStatus 5 — Progress, Completed, Failed, Abandoned, Uncertain; CancelOutcome 3 — Stopped, Completed, Uncertain (event.rs:278-292).

SESSION: SessionState 6 — Launching, Started, Ready, Blocked, Exited, Unknown (api.rs:1745-1758). INVITATION: 4 — Pending, Expired, Revoked, Redeemed (crates/locust-proto/src/api/invitations.rs:63-68).

WORKSPACE: WorkspaceAuthority 5 — Uninitialized, Pending, Ready, Disputed, Invalid (crates/locust-proto/src/api/workspace.rs:102-108); WorkspaceProposalStatus 7 — PendingAuthority, Disputed, ContentUnavailable, AwaitingEvidence, Stale, Ready, Integrated (api/workspace.rs:195-203); WorkspaceOperationState 3 — Prepared, Recorded, Completed (api/workspace.rs:78-86).

CONTENT object: BlobState 4 — Held, Requested, Unavailable, Unknown (api.rs:1669-1678). PENDING work: 7 kinds — ToAuthorize, ToStart, Claimed, HeldElsewhere, ToAcknowledge, ToReview, Deliveries (crates/locust-proto/src/api/context.rs:185-193).
halts_and_refusals: Halt kinds in the state machine, 4: Fork { seq, events }, BrokenChain { event }, Successors { previous, events }, IncompatibleProof { event } (crates/locust-core/src/goal/standing.rs:61-76). Fork and BrokenChain come from the administrator chain (goal/chain.rs:67,225) and halt the whole goal; Successors and IncompatibleProof come from the fold (goal/fold.rs:739,758) and halt one decision scope.

Halt kinds in the API, 2: AuthorityConflict (the only one produced; all 4 internal kinds map to it, node/views.rs:39-45 and requests/goals.rs:197-206) and SignerRecovery (declared, never produced) (crates/locust-proto/src/api.rs:1469-1478).

What a halt actually blocks: only the administrator's own signing, and any author whose own log forked or has gaps (goal/mod.rs:259-267). Other members keep signing ordinary work. The Halted error code is returned in exactly one place, goal.invite (node/requests/invitations.rs:186-191); other signing attempts in a halted goal come back as Unavailable.

Stall: there is no concept named stall. The nearest thing is an event held as Pending with one of 6 waiting reasons: Predecessor, Anchor, Reference, Definition, ForkProof, Evidence (standing.rs:17-24), backed by 3 kinds of missing dependency: Event, Definition, Content (standing.rs:10-14).

Exclusion reasons for an event, 8: NotAMember, PastRemoval, AnchorRegressed, NotAdministrator, BadEpoch, InvalidDefinition, Precondition(reason text), AfterHalt (standing.rs:27-36). Precondition carries a free-text reason; about 80 call sites in crates/locust-core/src/goal produce one.

Peer refusals on the wire, 6: UnsupportedVersion, NotAMember, InvitationRefused, LimitExceeded, ProtocolError, KeyUnavailable (crates/locust-proto/src/sync.rs:262-278). An exchange ends one of 3 ways: Completed, Refused(refusal), Aborted (crates/locust-core/src/sync/driver.rs:39-47).

API error codes, 15: Denied, NotFound, Invalid, Conflict, ClaimHeld, Superseded, IdempotencyMismatch, LimitExceeded, Unavailable, Halted, UnsupportedVersion, Corrupted, Internal, AuthorizationRequired, ReadOnly (api.rs:1843-1888). ReadOnly is never produced in non-test code.

Structural event rejections, 11: TooLarge, Malformed, NotCanonical, UnsupportedVersion, BadSequence, BadReferences, BadAnchor, BadPayloadLength, AuthorMismatch, BadSignature, IdMismatch (crates/locust-proto/src/event.rs:693-719).
Wait outcomes, 3: Work, NoEvent, Disconnected (api.rs:1730-1741); the CLI maps the last two to exit status 20 and 21 (crates/locust/src/cli/mod.rs:402-406).

Daemon self-fence: after a storage commit with unknown outcome the node sets `failed`, answers Internal "storage failed; restart the daemon" and stops (crates/locust-core/src/node/commit.rs:219-251, node/mod.rs:348-359). The SQLite store likewise refuses every call until reopened (crates/locust-store/src/lib.rs:27-36).
Hello refusals for a local client: Denied (unknown or revoked credential), UnsupportedVersion, Invalid (viewer credential with a session) (api.rs:317-345).
local_files: State directory $LOCUST_HOME or ~/.locust, mode 0700 (layout table at crates/locust-proto/src/local.rs:10-21; created and checked at crates/locust/src/daemon/home.rs:33-61,110-128).
daemon.sock — Unix socket; removed on clean stop (home.rs:79-107).
daemon.lock — lock held by the one running daemon; contains its process number (home.rs:131-165).

locust.db (+ locust.db-wal; no -shm because of exclusive locking) — SQLite, schema marker 6, four tables: goals, events, blobs, local (crates/locust-store/src/schema.rs:6,23-54). No migrations; any other format is refused.
blobs/<hash-hex> — content objects larger than 262,144 bytes; blobs/<hash>.staged — partially received objects (crates/locust-store/src/lib.rs:10-11, schema.rs:18-21).
logs/ — daemon and adapter logs (stdout.log, stderr.log when run as a service; crates/locust/src/installation/service.rs:234-235).
owner.credential — the person's 32-byte bearer secret, mode 0600 (home.rs:47-53).
agents/<name>.credential — one 32-byte bearer secret per enrolled agent; authors/<name>.credential for formation authors (crates/locust/src/cli/mod.rs:350-359).
sessions/<instance>.secret — one 32-byte secret per execution session (local.rs:206; or any absolute path via --session / LOCUST_SESSION).
context-receipts/<credential-digest>/<session>/<hash>.json — client-side cache of daemon-signed context receipts (crates/locust/src/context_receipts.rs:55-69,129).
onboarding/<id>/state.json with credential and session files, plus onboarding.lock (crates/locust/src/installation/onboarding.rs:107-123,280).

Inside locust.db, the `local` table has 13 record spaces (crates/locust-proto/src/store.rs:74-104): Identity, Agent, Goal, Peer, Invite, Claim, Cursor, Idempotency, Pending, Session, Blob, Key, Formation.
Space Identity: the endpoint secret (transport key seed), the owner credential digest, the last endpoint id and contact hints (crates/locust-core/src/node/identity.rs:20-22).
Space Agent: one record per agent with name, signing seed, credential digest, grants, revoked, author_only; one per viewer credential (identity.rs:75-84,115-121).

Space Goal, 10 record kinds per goal: revision counter, title, standing grants, checkout binding, workspace operation, join in progress (holds the invitation secret), task authorization, took-part/left flag, last sync per endpoint, farm publication record including the farm upload key seed (crates/locust-core/src/node/local.rs:26-33,174-180; node/farm.rs:22-45).

Space Key: one plaintext symmetric content key per goal per epoch (crates/locust-core/src/node/entry.rs:38-44). Space Invite: issued invitations by secret digest. Space Claim: session claims and generations. Space Cursor: feed positions and context acknowledgments. Space Idempotency: request key, digest and stored first response. Space Pending: effect delivery outbox/inbox. Space Session: adapter session records. Space Blob: which goals an object belongs to, withdrawn marks. Space Peer: contact hints and last sync time. Space Formation: drafts, presentations, publications.
All private key material (agent signing seeds, endpoint secret, content keys, farm seeds) sits unencrypted in locust.db; only the bearer credentials and session secrets are separate files.

Outside the state directory, written by install/setup/service commands and never by the daemon: <prefix>/install.lock, <prefix>/current, <prefix>/releases/<manifest-sha256>/ (crates/locust/src/installation.rs:194,231,261-262); <prefix>/setup/<id>.json and <id>.intent.json (installation/setup.rs:141-142); <prefix>/service-<label>.json (installation/service_install.rs:126); ~/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist or ~/.config/systemd/user/<label>.service (installation/service.rs:211-215); client MCP config files such as .codex/config.toml, .claude.json, .mcp.json (crates/locust/src/cli/client.rs:511-517).
Workspace checkouts are ordinary directories the person names; their bindings and in-flight operations live in Space Goal, not in the directory.
background_behaviors: On start: creates and locks the state directory, creates the owner credential and (first start) the endpoint secret, opens SQLite with a full checkpoint and orphan-file cleanup, rebuilds every goal from its event log, and runs pending flow effects for each goal before serving (crates/locust/src/daemon/mod.rs:103-141; crates/locust-core/src/node/mod.rs:104-190).

Brings up the peer transport: binds an iroh endpoint from the endpoint secret, by default with n0 relays, local-network and mainline-DHT lookup and port mapping on; records its endpoint id and contact hints (crates/locust/src/daemon/network.rs:59-103; node/peers.rs:63-71). Overridable with LOCUST_RELAY, LOCUST_LOOKUP, LOCUST_BIND.

Every second polls the sync driver (network.rs:156-157,313). The driver opens an exchange with every other current member's endpoint for every goal when the goal changed, at least every 30 s per goal-endpoint pair regardless (anti-entropy), and retries failures with backoff from 1 s doubling to 60 s (crates/locust-core/src/sync/driver.rs:15-21). Exchanges idle for 30 s are dropped (network.rs:30).

Within each exchange, unasked: reconciles events per author, then fetches the founding text, missing content keys, missing content objects in 1 MiB chunks, and pushes effect deliveries and collects receipts (stages at crates/locust-core/src/sync/initiator.rs:45-54).
Serves incoming exchanges from endpoints bound to current members; refuses everyone else with NotAMember, including for unknown goals (crates/locust-proto/src/sync.rs:52-60).

Admits joiners without asking: when a join request with a valid, unexpired, unrevoked invitation arrives, it signs MemberAdmitted with the administrator's key, provided that agent is active and holds `administer` and `manage_goals` (crates/locust-core/src/node/peers.rs:304-382).
Keeps presenting its own pending joins to the inviter until admitted or refused, and records a refusal (peers.rs:224-250,277-289).
Spreads fork evidence: sends the two conflicting events to every endpoint that was ever admitted, and stores valid evidence it receives (peers.rs:92-177).

Runs formation flow after every commit: signs EffectMaterialized for each due effect whose runner is a local agent holding the `flow` grant, which opens tasks, makes offers and requests reviews (crates/locust-core/src/node/flow.rs:11-47; node/commit.rs:140-152).
After every commit also clears completed joins and projects per-recipient delivery records (commit.rs:214-217; node/delivery.rs:47-60).

Publishes to the farm service: every second, for each goal with publication on, it builds the public snapshot, signs it with the farm key and sends upload, check-in, suspend or delete over HTTPS (default https://locust.farm), suspending by itself when the goal becomes ineligible; 20 s per exchange, own retry schedule (crates/locust/src/daemon/farm.rs:17-82; crates/locust-core/src/node/farm.rs:797-830).
Holds parked `wait` requests and answers them when the goal changes or the timeout passes (crates/locust/src/daemon/connection.rs:140-165).
Stores the first result of every request that carries an idempotency key (commit.rs:117-131).

Stops on SIGINT, SIGTERM or daemon.stop with a 5 s drain; fences itself and stops after a storage failure (crates/locust/src/daemon/mod.rs:190-200; crates/locust/src/daemon/shell.rs:17; commit.rs:219-251).

Things it does not do by itself today: launch or wake agent clients (client run is an explicit command), remove a member who asked to leave, rotate keys other than on member.remove, expire or garbage-collect history, take backups, or change any grant.
formal_models: research/tla/Organization.tla (245 lines; 33 cases: 16 safety, 9 witness, 8 mutation) — the replicated organization subset: every delivery order of a signed transcript, one administrator log, admission cutoffs, pinned definitions and rules, distinct reviewer identities, scope-local exact selection proofs, fork and double-successor halts, replay equals projection. Excludes documents, general selectors, close/reopen, encrypted epochs, wire decoding and transport (header at lines 4-18).

research/tla/AttemptSessions.tla (265 lines; 11 cases: 2 safety, 8 witness, 1 mutation) — local attempts and sessions on one daemon: claim generations, principal binding, local permission as a boolean input, idempotent retries, uncertain-commit fencing, memory matches store.

research/tla/FlowEffects.tla (135 lines; 8 cases: 1 safety, 5 witness, 2 mutation) — daemon-driven effects: logical identity independent of signature, deduplication, durable outbox, delivery versus acknowledgment versus start, retraction.

research/tla/Workspace.tla (278 lines; 54 cases: 26 safety, 18 witness, 10 mutation; registered as `proposed-safety`) — shared file tree authority: epoch checkpoints, explicit RetainBefore restoration, handoff fencing, source-author exclusion, authority independent of content availability.
research/tla/fixtures/RunnerFixture.tla (2 cases) — tests the checker runner only.

Registry and tooling: research/tla/cases.json lists 108 cases; research/tla/configs holds 106 .cfg files (plus an empty v1 directory); TLC 1.7.4 pinned in research/tla/toolchain.json; run by scripts/check_tla.py. These are bounded exhaustive checks; the README states no deductive proof and no proof that the Rust refines the models (research/tla/README.md:3-8).

Not modelled anywhere: peer reconciliation and transport, invitations and joining, content-key epochs and encryption, owner-to-agent grants beyond a boolean input, farm publication, and store crash recovery (those are covered by Rust tests and the in-tree simulator instead).

baseline.notes:
Scope: read-only inventory of the system as it stands; I ran no cargo, npm, build or test, and changed nothing in the repository. Two throwaway counting scripts live in the session scratchpad only. This return does not assess the plan itself.

Judgements made
- Signed record kinds = variants of `Body` (crates/locust-proto/src/event.rs:396-499): 25. By area: membership 4 (Genesis, MemberAdmitted, MemberRemoved, LeaveRequested), rules 1, tasks and work 9, evidence and decisions 4, documents 1, workspace 2, flow 2, farm publication 2. Four other signed structures exist outside that enum and are not in the 25: the invitation ticket (invite.rs:233-239), JoinRequest (invite.rs:388-398), SignedFarmRequest with 4 operations (crates/locust-proto/src/farm.rs:422-452), and the local-only ContextReceipt (crates/locust-proto/src/api/context.rs:52-59). Release bundles are also signed with a separate package key (crates/locust/src/package.rs:398), unrelated to goals.
- API requests = variants of `Request` (crates/locust-proto/src/api.rs:399-808): 97, confirmed two ways (serde rename tags and the operations table at api.rs:893-991). 40 read-only, 57 writing; 69 name a goal; 63 are offered to the model as MCP tools. There are 50 response variants (api.rs:1286).
- Leaf command = a command path that runs on its own. That gives 136 tree leaves plus `pending`, which runs by itself and also has a `page` subcommand: 137. Derived by reading the builders (crates/locust/src/cli/args.rs:150-324 and the per-area files in crates/locust/src/cli/) and cross-checked against the checked-in export docs/reference/generated/runtime.contract.json, which has the same 136 leaves. 64 of the 137 are generated one-to-one from API operations (args.rs:240-279); 73 are hand-written (68 static plus goal add-local, daemon run, agent add, agent enroll, author enroll). `call` is counted once although it reaches all 97 operations; `mcp` once although it serves 63 tools. The 7 global flags (--home, --credential, --owner, --as, --session, --json, --idempotency-key) are not counted. 33 API operations have no generated command and are reached through hand-written commands, `call` or MCP: farm.* 5, invitation.* 4, permission.* 5, workspace.* 14, inbox, formation.validate, formation.explain, agent.enroll, author.enroll.

Facts worth carrying into the comparison
- Baseline for grants and delegation is zero signed records: the person has no key and every person-to-agent permission is an unsigned local row.
- A computer has no identity in a goal beyond the endpoint written into a member's admission; one endpoint per admission.
- Wire sync has 17 frame kinds (crates/locust-proto/src/sync.rs:301-372) and 6 refusals.
- Declared but unused today: Halt::SignerRecovery and ErrorCode::ReadOnly appear only in the API definition and CLI rendering (api.rs:1477,1887; crates/locust/src/cli/presentation.rs:54; crates/locust/src/failure.rs:30).
- Two overlapping grant APIs coexist (goal.grant vs permission.allow/revoke; task.authorize vs permission.task.allow).

Small inconsistencies noticed in passing

items.name: Stage recipients
items.what: Worked out from members and roles at the anchor where the effect was signed. Today they are the members at the rules binding (goal/flow.rs:59-62).

items.name: Automatic plan selection
items.what: The host's daemon signs scope_decided for each agreed document when a revision is next. It reads no level, takes the lowest id among the revisions it holds and reads the evaluation again before each signing. The plan calls it the fourth automatic act.

items.name: Automatic file acceptance
items.what: The host's daemon signs scope_decided at workspace scope for the first due proposal in id order that passes two local gates, then looks again until none passes. The first files are signed in the request that posts them. A fifth automatic act.

items.name: Gates inside the daemon
items.what: Before each acceptance the daemon checks that the content is complete on its computer and that no path is private. is_denied and its lists move from locust-workspace (select.rs:18-62) to locust-proto. Today the private-path refusal runs only in the command line, at the accept step that is removed.

items.name: Stalled-step reporting
items.what: For each selection the daemon wants, it works out the first failing test where it holds the host's agent, and RunnerElsewhere where it does not.

items.name: Roles are read at each act's anchor
items.what: Every daemon must resolve rules per (context, anchor) alike in any arrival order. About ten call sites pass an anchor and two look ahead from the head. The formal model does not cover it until Phase 7. Eleven signed-replay tests.

items.name: One holder per deciding role
items.what: Kept only by the host's daemon before it signs, not by replay. If a deciding list ever held two members nobody would decide until the host gave the role again.

items.name: Latest review, pinned and unpinned
items.what: Two answers every daemon must compute alike: unpinned (each member's latest effective review by seq in its own log, can go from yes to no) and pinned (a decision keeps the approvals its record pinned). Includes a reviewer whose log forks. Seven tests.

items.name: Only member judged at an anchor the author chooses
items.what: Rests on two signer-side facts, not replay rules: only a host's agent is ever alone, and the host agent's log holds every governance record, which bounds how far back it can anchor. One residual case is stated. Seven tests.

items.name: First-files rule
items.what: Decided by three facts of one record and the goal's first record; once per epoch that starts empty; never disagrees with the only-member part; only the person posts it (signer-side check). The workspace model is not extended for it by any phase. Seven tests.

items.name: Order of decisions in a scope
items.what: Sorted by (anchor position, author, seq, id), because the deciding member can change. Today by the author's seq alone (goal/projection.rs:344-350).

items.name: Agreed document stream
items.what: The same text on every daemon in any arrival order; base check; one successor per predecessor; an excluded host decision stops the stream until the next rules bind. The formal model does not cover document streams. Five replay tests and five two-daemon tests.

items.name: Tie between two counting changes
items.what: For the plan and for files, the host's computer records the lowest identifier among those it holds, so arrival there decides which lands. Other daemons check validity only. The loser is rebuilt and approved again. Questions 9 and 13 are open.

items.name: One acceptance per head across restarts
items.what: A restart between deciding and signing never yields two successors. A second record at a used position of the host's log halts governance for good (measured on today's code). Depends on the restore guard. Thirteen new daemon-level tests in R9.

items.name: Host-only gates and no blocking
items.what: The content and private-path gates are the host daemon's checks, not replay rules: a peer's valid acceptance of unreadable content is still accepted. A change that fails a gate never holds back one that passes.

items.name: R10 recipes
items.what: Six two-daemon recipes with expected output kept under research/: first files; competing changes on files and on the plan; approve then reject; missing content; stop and start; a host restored from an old copy. No product code and no new tests.

hardest: goal/fold.rs: rule resolution becomes keyed by (context, anchor) with about ten callers that must each pass the right position, and predicate splits into an unpinned answer (each member's latest review, which can go from yes to no) and a pinned one, so one wrong anchor or one missed fork case makes two daemons disagree on whether a result counts.

node/flow.rs: the host's daemon signs plan selections and file acceptances unattended (R8, R9), where a second successor at a used log position halts governance for good, so the re-read before each signing, the pass-over loop at the two gates, restarts, a reject arriving before or after, and the restore guard must all leave at most one record per predecessor.

The rules that rest on a check the host's daemon makes before signing and not on replay (only a host's agent is ever the only member, only the person posts first files, a deciding role has one holder), judged at an anchor the author chooses and bounded by the host agent's log holding every governance record, which K1 moves to another key before R4 is built without the text being revised.

By reason: 27 items trace to a numbered owner decision (2, 5, 6, 7, 15, 16, 17), 10 are safety, 28 could be cut or deferred. The cuttable ones fall in five groups: (a) the separate role_holders record with roles read at each act, lists that never end and a fixed role kind; (b) the whole of R8, the plan settling by itself; (c) a role on an invitation; (d) count and exclude_author on a check; (e) the preset and role renames. The owner's decisions alone require: the only-member part and the peer-review default (5), latest review (6), member names (17), removal of the integrator with automatic file acceptance (15), and first files (16).

R8 is not an owner decision, but R9 is written on top of it: R9 takes Evaluation.desired_selections, Step, Stall::RunnerElsewhere and the rule that automatic acts read no level from R8 (plan lines 3441-3446). Cutting R8 moves those four into R9.

ledgers.notes:
Sources. Plan text: scratch/safety.json (cited as safety.json with piece key KEY, GUARD or END, phase and bullet; seams by number). Master plan: docs/master-plan.md. Code cites are in the working tree of ., which other sessions were editing (chain.rs, driver.rs and farm.rs are modified and uncommitted). The plan document docs/host-safety-and-ending-plan.md is not in the repository. Nothing was built or run.

Counts (78 items): signed_format 7 adds, 4 changes; local_state 5 adds, 1 change; states 12 adds, 4 changes, 3 removes; surface 12 adds, 6 changes, 1 remove; background 7 adds, 4 changes; invariants 11 adds. By reason: 45 owner decision, 20 safety, 13 cuttable. In plain numbers the piece adds 1 kind of signing key, 1 signed record kind, 1 protocol step, 6 kinds of on-disk state (one secret per hosted goal, one directory outside the data directory, four records), 2 commands, 2 requests, 1 sync refusal, 1 refusal side, 2 reachable Halt values (one new, one declared today and never set), 1 new TLA model and 10 new model cases. No exit code number is new; exit 9 for read_only exists and is unreachable today. E1 to E3 store nothing new on disk.

Where the complexity sits. The restore guard (G1, G2) is the largest part on every measure: 5 of the 6 on-disk additions, 7 of the 12 new states, 6 of the 7 new background behaviours, the only new model, and about 40 percent of the lines. K1 is small in new concepts and wide in files (about 26 non-test files, about 110 fixture sites). E1 is one record and one gate, with three end states. E3 is self-contained.

Cuttable without contradicting an owner decision: all of E3 (the plan says the first public door does not wait for it); host steps on the governance key (S: host_may_sign); the AfterEnd rule for records anchored at the end; Halt::SignerConflict; the doctor check; the status line for a copy older than a goal; E2's waiting entry and remove line; the agent revoke lines; the counterexample traces. Required for safety but not asked for by the owner: the hold on agent keys and on newly admitted keys, the call-back of unknown callers, revoking invitations on a restore, refusing the person's own commands while catching up, 'ended, then halted', 'end held but not in force', and the models. guard_attest (the farm-service check, decision 21) is specified in G1 and built with the public-goals plan; it is not counted here.

Contradictions and silences.
1. Decision 14 (master-plan.md:86-87) says a member whose agent signs a leave is removed by the host's computer automatically. E2's checked text says 'Nothing is removed automatically' and builds a 'Waiting for you' entry with a remove command; the build-order row for E2 (master-plan.md:211) also says only 'The host sees who asked to leave'. No text says which code path signs the removal, how it passes the guard, the ended test and a halt, or whether WaitingKind::AskedToLeave stays. K1 states the governance key signs unattended 'in two places only'; this makes three. I counted the automatic removal as one background addition and put its code only in the high figures.
2. Decision 9 says the key 'does nothing else'. K1 also has it sign stage steps, and from R8 and R9 the plan's text and landed file changes. K1 lists this as its first owner question; it is not answered in the master plan.
3. The phase texts in safety.json predate the seam fixes. Where they differ I counted the fix: Node::signs_alone is deleted (seam 7), GoalSummary.guard is a list (seam 11), E3 depends on G1 (seam 12; its text says 'Nothing'), E1 does not add GoalEnded to eligible (seam 10), revoke_pending is G1's (seam 9).
4. The plan gives no line estimate for E1, E2 or E3.
5. The marks file has a magic header and no version number, while decision 2 relies on a number to refuse old formats.
6. G1's start table rests on file identity that the plan says nobody measured.

Removals the plan lists that are not in today's code and so are not counted: the sentence 'the host agent is disconnected; nothing can sign for this goal' and the warning 'freeze for everyone' (they exist only in docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:649 and :988), G1's two fixed read_only sentences (replaced in G2), and 'signing watermarks' (a comment at crates/locust-proto/src/store.rs:75 for state that never existed).

code.basis: The eight line figures are Rust only, to match the 103,000-line baseline. Not in those figures: the site (TypeScript, Svelte, CSS) +950 to +1,450 non-test, -100 to -170, tests +450 to +650; the Python harness +1,000 to +1,700. files_touched counts every kind of file. Scope counted: J0 to J6, J8 and the first-end part of J7, as corrected by the 13 review findings and by answers 17 to 24. Not counted: J7's takeover parts (replacing a host comes after v2, docs/master-plan.md:7) and the notice to a removed computer (left out on purpose, docs/master-plan.md:241-244).

Totals: 88 items. signed_format 9, local_state 12, states 17, surface 22, background 15, invariants 13. 67 added, 16 changed, 5 removed. New keys: none. New secrets on disk: none. Built today versus new. Built: the farm service with signed upload, check-in, suspend and delete, receipts, the operator allowlist, the gallery with an Ended filter, the event stream, and deletion 30 days after an end (crates/locust-farm/src/lib.rs, about 1,060 non-test and 1,910 test lines); the page types and the signed publication and consent records (crates/locust-proto/src/farm.rs, 774 lines); the publisher, consent and projection (crates/locust-core/src/node/farm.rs, 965); farm on, off, show, status and consent (crates/locust/src/cli/farm.rs, 241); the farm page, gallery and map on the site (about 2,150 lines); single-use invitations; six presets. ledgers.piece: Replacing a host (after v2): first version with one optional backup host, and the later threshold step
ledgers.one_line: A host may name one member as backup host; that member's computer can sign one takeover record with a fresh key, naming the last host record it holds, after which everything the old host signed later is void on every computer, except the old host's removal of that backup, which voids the takeover.

items.name: Record kind: backup host named
items.what: One governance record by which the host names one member as backup host, in clear and outside the sealed formation. At least 2 fields: the member, and a rule slot whose only value is "alone". Record kinds go from 25 today (7 governance; crates/locust-proto/src/event.rs:396-503) to 27 with the next item. Provisional: the note does not fix the fields or say how a backup is un-named.

items.name: Record kind: takeover
items.what: One record at position 0 of a new key's log. At least 4 fields: base (event id of the last host record the backup holds), cutoff (a point in the old key's log, which may be any event), the member who is now host, and an endorsement by the backup's agent key. Provisional: field list is the design round's, not decided.

items.name: A fresh signing key per host term
items.what: Each takeover creates a new key that signs membership and rules from then on. Today one key signs for the life of a goal (crates/locust-core/src/goal/history.rs:146 holds a single administrator). The backup's agent key also gains a second use: endorsing the takeover. Counted once here; it is also one more unencrypted secret on the taking computer's disk per takeover per goal.

items.name: Invitation names an issuer beside the goal's root key
items.what: Plus 1 signed field. Today the invitation has one field for both (crates/locust-proto/src/invite.rs:114-117: "the goal's administrator, which in the current protocol is also the issuer"). Without it a host of a later term cannot invite anyone, because the goal id still hashes the first key.

items.name: Protocol version 8
items.what: One version number, 7 to 8. Under decision 2 it ends every goal made under v2, public ones included.

items.name: Planned handoff by a present host
items.what: Either the takeover record gains the old host's signed consent (plus 1 field, plus 1 signer) or no format change (the host names, the other person takes). The note lists both and chooses neither. No owner decision asks for a planned handoff; decision 8 names only a host that disappears.

items.name: Content keys stored by removal record id
items.what: The key store is indexed by goal and epoch number today (crates/locust-core/src/node/entry.rs:27-28, 38-51; crates/locust-core/src/node/replica.rs:216-217). It becomes indexed by the id of the removal that opened the key, and keys of voided branches are kept, so a computer can hold more than one key for one epoch number.

items.name: Per-endpoint marker that the takeover notice was delivered
items.what: Needed by the rule that the previous host cannot be removed until the notice has reached it. One marker per endpoint ever admitted, per takeover. Provisional: the note states the rule and one reviewer's "keep a delivered record per endpoint"; no store is designed.

items.name: Standing: excluded, superseded
items.what: A ninth exclusion kind beside the 8 today (crates/locust-core/src/goal/standing.rs:27-36). Applies to every old-key record after the cutoff and to work anchored there, whenever delivered.

items.name: Goal state: host term
items.what: A goal has terms 0, 1, 2 and so on, each with one signing key. Who the host is becomes a function of position in the chain instead of a constant read from the first record.

items.name: Member standing: backup host
items.what: A member named as backup and not yet acted. Must be a member at the base.

items.name: Member standing: previous host
items.what: After a takeover the old host stays a member and cannot be removed until the notice has reached it or the person confirms the loss.

items.name: Takeover standing: void because the removal surfaced
items.what: A takeover that is in force stops being in force on a computer when that computer receives the old host's removal of the backup. The backup's computer must then stop signing with the term key. The note does not define the standing of records the voided term signed or of work anchored at them.

items.name: Receipt outcome: takeover record ignored
items.what: A takeover record that cannot be fully checked from what a computer holds is dropped, never held as pending. This is a new outcome beside the 6 waiting kinds (crates/locust-core/src/goal/standing.rs:17-24).

items.name: Term in dispute after two takeovers (not sized)
items.what: One restore of the backup's computer from before its takeover produces a second takeover of the same term. The note offers five competing fixes and the owner has not chosen (question 4). Adds 0 states if a restored copy re-creates the identical record, 1 or more if a dispute state or a superseding field is chosen.

items.name: Per-record mark: the backup has seen it or has not
items.what: For each removal and admission, derived from the backup's anchors, with no new record. A backup that signs nothing shows every recent record as unseen.

items.name: Work built on a voided record is excluded, not left waiting
items.what: Today such an event returns Pending(Anchor) or AnchorRegressed and every later event of that author walks through it (crates/locust-core/src/goal/chain.rs:418-438). The walk changes for the superseded case so the author's next event on the kept chain is judged normally.

items.name: A forked host log is no longer a permanent halt
items.what: Today a second record at a used position sets Halt::Fork and no code clears it (crates/locust-core/src/goal/chain.rs:222-233; crates/locust-core/src/goal/history.rs:83-87). A backup can take over from the branch it holds. Provisional: confirmed by the reviewers for the successor design, not restated in section 8.

items.name: Command and request: name a backup host
items.what: 1 command and 1 API request, 2 if un-naming is separate (97 API operations today, crates/locust-proto/src/api.rs:892). No command name is chosen in the note.

items.name: Explicit command to name someone who came through the public door
items.what: 1 command or flag. The note's section 8 says door members may not be named; decision 19 is later and wins.

items.name: Command and requests: take over
items.what: 1 command, 1 to 2 API requests. Shows the base, which members were heard from, and what is dropped, then asks for one confirmation that also covers the new host's first two records.

items.name: Override: confirm the previous host is lost
items.what: 1 flag or prompt that lets the new host remove the previous host before the notice has reached it.

items.name: Refusal kinds
items.what: 4: caller is not the named backup; the previous host cannot be removed yet; a joiner's admission was voided and it must ask for a new ticket; a ticket issued by an earlier host is dead. A fifth is proposed and not adopted: refuse a takeover when no member was heard from. The note names no exit code (15 error codes today, crates/locust/src/failure.rs:123-138).

items.name: Words a person must learn
items.what: 3: "backup host", "take over", and a word for what is lost ("dropped" in the proposed sentence, `superseded` in the API).

items.name: Status lines
items.what: Who the backup host is, that this computer is the backup, that a takeover happened and what was dropped, and on the old host's computer that it is no longer host. Count not fixed by the note; at least 4 lines.

items.name: Invitations, the door and the public page do not carry over
items.what: After a takeover the new host issues invitations again and a public goal gets a new address; the old page cannot be updated or taken down by anyone (upload seed is on the old disk: crates/locust-core/src/node/farm.rs:23, 55). The person does these by hand. The alternative, deriving the page seed from the signing key, is not chosen (question 8).

items.name: Dial every reachable member before choosing the base
items.what: The taking computer syncs with each member it can reach and reports who answered. A daemon rule, not a validity rule; a member that under-reports what it holds steers the base and the note found no way to detect it.

items.name: Push the takeover notice to every endpoint ever admitted

Counts are of what the note's section 8 and owner decisions 10, 11, 12 and 19 require, measured against today's code, minus what v2 builds first.

First-version totals (provisional). Signed format: 2 record kinds (25 to 27), at least 7 signed fields, 1 new signing key per takeover, 1 version number; 1 more field if the planned handoff is kept. Local state: 1 store re-indexed, 1 new marker, 1 more secret per takeover. States: 7 added, 2 changed, 1 not sized. Surface: 3 to 5 commands, 4 to 6 API requests, 4 refusal kinds, 3 words, at least 4 status lines, no exit code named. Background: 4 things added, 2 changed, 1 cuttable. Invariants: 4 delivery properties, 2 new models, 3 changed models, 2 further properties, 18 scenarios. Removals: none. I found nothing in today's code that the first version deletes outright; every touch to an existing construct is a change. The two refusals "the administrator cannot leave / remove itself before authority handoff" (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/goals.rs:265, 293) stay for a host that has not handed off.

Later step (threshold among named people), on top: 2 record kinds, M more signing keys, 4 states, at least 4 commands, 3 scenarios, 700 to 1,500 non-test and 1,200 to 2,500 test lines. The master plan lists it under "left out on purpose for now" (line 243).

Baseline cannot be read. docs/host-safety-and-ending-plan.md is not in the repository, so what K1, G1 and G2 leave behind is unknown. If K1 reads the host key from the first record as a constant, the takeover must revisit every reader of it. Items the note's section 8 lists that v2 already builds are not counted here: the dedicated key (K1) and the catch-up gate (G1, G2).

Schedule dependency. Build-order row 14 (R8) needs "the takeover record's shape decided" (docs/master-plan.md:213), so part of this design round sits inside v2 although the piece follows v2.

Contradictions.
1. Note line 894 says door members may not be named; decision 19 says the host may name one with an explicit command. Decision 19 is later and wins.
2. Note lines 959-961 require that an in-force takeover is never undone by a later delivery; decision 12 undoes one. The invariant must be restated.
3. Decision 10 says a takeover fixes "the last host record"; the note's item 5 lets the cutoff be any event of the old key's log, and owner question 5 is unanswered. Which key signs the R8 and R9 recordings under K1 decides whether one cutoff is enough.

Silent.
- Decision 12 covers removal of the backup. It does not cover the host naming a different backup after the base (owner question 3 asked about both).
- The standing of records signed by a term that is later voided, and of work anchored at them.
- Command names, exit codes, the form of a planned handoff, the cap on takeover records per endorser.
- Whether the key request on the wire must name the removal record; today it names the bare epoch (crates/locust-proto/src/sync.rs:332) and two reviewers disagree.

Open problems that add state or protocol the count cannot size.
- A fresh content key at takeover. Today a new key is made only on a removal and the epoch is the count of removals (chain.rs:76-80; payloads sign `key_epoch: u32`, event.rs:38-42). After a takeover the old host and anyone it admitted past the base still hold the current key. One reviewer asks for a rotation record in the first version; the design defers it. It would add 1 record kind, a new definition of epoch and a key hand-out step. Not in any figure above.
- Telling the old host. Counted only as one message kind, one push and one marker. Frame contents, bound, retries, what a twice-replaced host needs, and the old host's own stop rule are not designed.
- Removals the backup never received. The note says no pure fix exists without acknowledgements, which the owner set aside. A removed member becomes a member again holding every key. Only display and prompts are proposed; none is sized beyond the one status mark.
- Two takeovers. Counted as one unsized state. The fix could be a derived key and a fixed timestamp, a field naming superseded candidates, or a permanent halt; each changes the record, the builder and the model differently.

Line numbers are from the checkout as read on 6 October 2026; chain.rs and other files had uncommitted edits by other sessions. Nothing was built or run.

Today, what decides whether one computer signs in one goal: membership (5: joining, member, removed, left, refused) x goal halted (2) x own log usable (2) x administrator here (2) x local agent revoked (2) = 80 raw combinations, about 20 that behave differently. The 128 grant combinations are settings, not states.

After v2, private goal: membership (5) x halt (4: none, authority conflict, signer recovery, signer conflict) x end (4: none, in force, held but not in force, ended then halted) x hold on the governance key (3: none, behind, unheard) x hold on the agent's key (4: none, behind, unheard, just admitted) x hosted here (2) x host's agent connected (2) x level (3) = 11,520 raw. Reachable is far lower: about 100 on a member's computer and on the order of 1,000 on the host's. A public goal multiplies the host's side by the door (6 states, 5 closed reasons, 2 causes of full: 12 readings) and the publisher (6 states): 829,440 raw. Per task there is also allowance (4) x who wrote it (2), and per member how it came in (3) and asked to leave (2).

Pairs the plans define (about 20): held with halted (signer recovery never over authority conflict); ended with held (seam 6); ended with halted; end held behind a missing record; held with the person's own commands, with a join, with a stage step, with farm off (seam 26); ended with farm off, with leave (refused), with asked-to-leave; halted with goal end (seam 24); host's agent disconnected with host commands and with workspace init (seam 3); forked agent key with a hold (seam 16); just admitted with a hold (seam 27); only member with a second admission and with a removal; door with halted, catching up, held, ended. 1. Catching up after a whole-computer restore x public goal with an absent door member: the hold never ends by itself (safety.json GUARD G1, second table).

Member asked to leave x host catching up, ended, halted or off: decision 14's removal has no design; meanwhile the leaver still counts for the only-member rule (docs/roles-and-permissions-plan.md:1836-1842), keeps its roles, keeps a place under the ceiling of 16, and is one of the computers a restored host must hear from.

top_risks: A permanent halt caused by the host's own computer. After K1, R4, R8, R9, decision 14 and the door, the governance key signs by itself in seven situations, three of which do not replay to the same record (file and plan acceptance pick the lowest id among what has arrived; a removal draws a fresh content key; an admission depends on who asked). One second record at a used position of that log stops membership and rules for good, and v2 cannot replace a host. The guard that prevents it has eight stated holes (safety.json GUARD G1, Risks), rests on file identity nobody measured and on sync behaviour that was read and not run, and in a public goal its release rule needs every stranger's computer to answer, so the forking override becomes the normal path.

Computers disagreeing on what counts. Six phases from four documents edit the same few functions (next_place, authorize_base, Chain::build, the find in drive_flow, plan_join), each written against a different commit (cfb5b45, f12eec8, c5201dd; HEAD is 67e8ac1), with their combined order written only in seam 20. On top of that R3 keeps a second copy of the fold's rules guarded by seven test rows against 51 sites in crates/locust-core/src/goal/fold.rs, R4 re-keys rule lookup by position at 22 call sites, and E1 adds three end states. A slip in any of them is not a crash; it is two honest computers holding different answers.

The door opening before its protections have an owner. The always-ask check for door members' tasks has no phase; nothing covers an auto reviewer reading strangers' work and R9 then landing it unattended; the default formation fails the door's safety check; J1 admits one phase before J2's check; the only-member and first-files exceptions change meaning after R4 is built; and strangers can drive unattended admissions, removals with key rotation (up to 1,024 seats) and unbounded Wanted records on other people's computers (research/joinable-farms-rewrite-contract-review-2026-10-05.md:43-120).

Building on text that is missing, stale or undecided. The host safety plan exists only as a JSON file in a scratch directory with 28 fixes pending; E2 contradicts decision 14; R4, R8 and R9 still describe the host's agent as the signer and are due for revision only after v2; R8, R9, R10 and the door wait on a takeover design that needs another round, an attack and a model; the public-goals phases are unwritten and their contract contradicts answers 18, 19, 20 and 22. Meanwhile nothing can be released until all sixteen phases land, the scripts and guides are broken from R1 to R6, and the frozen vectors are regenerated five times.

Proof that does not arrive. The plan promises a model per piece and delivers one new model, estimated at a day, that needs the repository's first liveness property; first files, document streams, one acceptance per head, door admission, the join-safety check and automatic removal get tests only, on top of sync, invitations and key epochs that were never modelled. The rest of the evidence needs people and hardware nobody has sized: five or more test readers, 8 and 16 real agents of different owners on different computers, two Macs, Time Machine and Migration Assistant restores, and a measured member ceiling that decides whether the door ships at 16, at 8 or not at all.

simplifications_already_in_plan: Permissions: one daemon-wide grant and seven per-goal grants (Grants and GoalGrants, crates/locust-proto/src/api.rs:349-365) plus a per-round task authorization become one level of three values and one task allowance. 128 switch combinations per agent per goal become 3.

Two overlapping grant interfaces become one: goal.grant beside permission.allow and permission.revoke, and task.authorize beside permission.task.allow (crates/locust-core/src/node/requests/goals.rs:238, requests/tasks.rs:167, requests/permissions.rs:152-180; api.rs:913, 940 and 983-989). Requests go from 97 to 89 after R3 and agent tools from 63 to 56. Four files of 70, 237, 300 and 261 lines are deleted (api/permissions.rs, node/requests/permissions.rs, cli/permissions.rs, cli/local_members.rs).

The scattered grant tests go: 11 require_grant and 4 authorization_required call sites in today's working tree under crates/locust-core/src/node are replaced by one check before every agent signature. (The ledger counted 14 and 2 at an earlier commit.)

The host's computer needs no grant for the host's unattended work: admission on an invitation loses its test of two grants (crates/locust-core/src/node/peers.rs:338-358) and stage steps lose the flow grant test (crates/locust-core/src/node/flow.rs:23). Today neither works until the owner sets grants.
Credential kinds drop from four to three: the viewer caller goes (Caller::Viewer, crates/locust-proto/src/api.rs:308).

The integrator seat goes with its setting, command, request, tool and stored operation: WorkspacePolicy.integrator (crates/locust-proto/src/organization.rs:127), `workspace integrate` (crates/locust/src/cli/workspace.rs:107 and 582), the request (api.rs:549 and 933) and the Integrate operation (crates/locust-proto/src/api/workspace.rs:63).

A goal gets one way to be over. Today a close on the goal scope marks the public page Ended and stops nothing (crates/locust-core/src/node/farm.rs:467-484). E1 replaces it with one end record, and page states drop from four to three (FarmGoalState::Disputed, crates/locust-proto/src/farm.rs:68-73).

Fewer things can halt a goal. Today a second record at any used position of the administrator's log halts governance, a forked review included (crates/locust-core/src/goal/chain.rs:222-233; test at goal/tests.rs:1602), and the administrator's agent must be connected for any change to members or rules (crates/locust-core/src/node/access.rs:81-96). After K1 only the governance key's own log can halt it, and disconnecting the working agent freezes nothing.

Two declarations that nothing produces today get a use instead of staying dead: Halt::SignerRecovery and ErrorCode::ReadOnly (api.rs:1477 and 1887; otherwise found only in the exit-code table at crates/locust/src/failure.rs:30 and one rendering arm at cli/presentation.rs:54).

Role holders stop travelling as JSON inside the rules record (`--roles`, from GoalCreate.roles and RulesBind.roles at api.rs:459 and 486; RulesBinding.roles at crates/locust-proto/src/event.rs:262); two commands replace it. Built-in role names go from three (coordinator, judge, reviewer in organization/presets.rs) to two.

Joining has one path and one way to confirm: `invitation join` (api.rs:772) and `goal add-local` fold into `goal join` and `goal add`, and the ticket's `--review` identifier (crates/locust/src/cli/invitations.rs:52) and `--yes` fold into one confirmation.
One view replaces three: `inbox` (api.rs:805 and 989), `permission inspect` and the seven grant rows fold into plain `status`.

On a public goal there is no separate consent step for a name (decision 17). Today the page is held back until every active member and every author has a consent record (crates/locust-core/src/node/farm.rs:124-150); afterwards only the host's decline suspends it.

In the public-goals groundwork (J0) the daemon stops writing a record for every completed exchange (the 's' record, crates/locust-core/src/node/peers.rs:20), and the shared 64 MiB budget for connections not yet admitted (crates/locust/src/daemon/network.rs:35) becomes a fixed small window per connection.
